chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from Ali, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, that he asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), saying:
Reciting quietly (I'dmar) is more beloved to me, and do not recite aloud, and that which indicates that this is only permissible in the state of precaution (Taqiyyah) and necessity, as he narrated.
ai.seo_question: Is it better to recite the Talbiyah quietly or aloud during Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) establishes a preference for the quiet recitation (Ismar) of the Talbiyah, reflecting the Shia emphasis on inner devotion and subtlety in worship. He clarifies that vocalizing it aloud remains valid, particularly in contexts of Taqiyyah or necessity, aligning with the broader jurisprudential principle that ease is granted where hardship might arise. This narration is pivotal in the chapter of Talbiyah recitation within al-Istibsar, illustrating the balance between recommended modesty and permissible public declaration.
